text:
Justin Sourdif scored one of the strangest goals of Washington's season, an Anthony Beauvillier shot that went in off him to make it 6-4 against Dallas, which Tom Gulitti of NHL.com noted changed who got charged with the loss in net. He's been a useful depth forward for the Capitals all year: three goals in 13 games at under 14 minutes a night.

The finishing is a bit hot (three goals on 2.1 expected, the quality of his chances), but Washington has 54% of the five-on-five expected goals with him on the ice, about even with the team.

Last season is the reason the Capitals trust him. Evolving-Hockey had him 42nd among 401 forwards in wins above replacement, with strong defense (91st percentile) and penalties drawn. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had 70% of his exits leaving the zone with possession and 19% of his setups coming from behind the net. He's 24, a third-round pick by Florida. Our projection sees about 15 goals.
